classification.difficultyReason: Match unbounded branches, unequal one-sided heights and an open point to the three supplied discontinuity categories; no calculation or additional representation is required.

content.prompt: The diagrams below show functions that have discontinuities. Categorise them as either jump discontinuities, holes, or asymptotic discontinuities.

spec.description: Two reciprocal-like branches, a dashed vertical asymptote right of the y-axis, the source numeral 1 beneath the positive x-axis, axis labels and direction arrows. Coordinates used for drawing are schematic; no equation or asymptote coordinate is supplied to students.
spec.mathematics: A vertical asymptotic discontinuity, with opposite unbounded behaviour on its two sides and branches approaching the horizontal axis.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph is visible; the classification appears only in answers.

answer.worked: The branches become unbounded as they approach the dashed vertical line. This is an asymptotic discontinuity.

spec.description: A leftward ray on y=0 has an open endpoint at the origin. A rightward ray on y=1 has a closed endpoint on the y-axis. The graph has axis labels, the height label 1 and ray arrows; no grid.
spec.mathematics: The left-hand value approaches 0 and the right-hand value approaches 1 at x=0.
spec.answerVisibility: Both rays and endpoint markers are permanent givens; the classification is hidden in the student edition.

answer.worked: At $x=0$, the left branch approaches $0$ and the right branch approaches $1$. These values differ, so there is a jump discontinuity.

spec.description: An upward-opening parabola with vertex at the origin, arrows at both upper ends and an open circle on its right branch. Neither the hole nor the axes has numerical coordinates printed. The plotting equation is an internal construction of the schematic parabola.
spec.mathematics: An otherwise continuous parabolic curve has one point removed.
spec.answerVisibility: The open circle is a permanent given; the classification appears only in answers.

answer.worked: The curve approaches the same point from both sides, but the open circle shows that this point is missing. The discontinuity is a hole.
